title: Abel Axe
blurb: The Abel Axe is an electric guitar invented by Jeff Abel from Wyoming, United States and engineered by James Jones. Made from aircraft grade T-6 Billet aluminium, its distinguishing features are the various sized holes dotting the body. All Abel Axes are made in the United States.

title: Alapini veena
blurb: Ālāpiṇī vīṇā and eka-tantrī vīṇā The ālāpiṇī vīṇā was a medieval stick-zither veena in India, with a single string and a gourd resonator. Later forms added more strings. The instruments became prominent in Indian music after 500 C.E. as instruments of court music.

title: Alghoza
about: Woodwind instrument used in South Asia
blurb: Alghoza also called Beenon is a paired woodwind traditional musical instrument of Sindhi culture, also used by Kutchi, Saraiki, Punjabi, Rajasthani and Baloch folk musicians. It consists of two joined beak flutes, one for melody, the second for drone.

title: Appalachian dulcimer
blurb: The Appalachian dulcimer is a fretted string instrument of the zither family, typically with three or four strings, originally played in the Appalachian region of the United States. The body extends the length of the fingerboard, and its fretting is generally diatonic.

title: Arched harp
blurb: Arched harps is a category in the Hornbostel-Sachs classification system for musical instruments, a type of harp. The instrument may also be called bow harp. With arched harps, the neck forms a continuous arc with the body and has an open gap between the two ends of the arc.

title: Autoharp
blurb: An autoharp is a string instrument in the zither family. Its distinctive structural feature is a set of bars, each with damping pads that mute the strings not belonging to a specified chord.

title: BeatBuddy
blurb: The BeatBuddy is a digital drum machine made by Singular Sound that is housed in the form of a stompbox unit. The floor-based format and pedal footswitch enable musicians to control the device hands-free while they are playing an instrument. Singular Sound is a Miami-based brand.

title: Bina Musical Stores
about: Wind and folk instruments from New Delhi
blurb: In New Delhi since 1950, Bina sells Indian instruments, including bamboo and brass flutes, the shehnai, the been (snake flute) and shruti boxes.

title: Bladder fiddle
blurb: The bladder fiddle was a folk instrument used throughout Europe and in the Americas. The instrument was originally a simple large stringed fiddle made with a long stick, one or more thick gut strings, and a pig's-bladder resonator. It was bowed with either a notched stick or a horsehair bow.

title: Bobbili veena
blurb: Bobbili veena is a large plucked string instrument used in Carnatic classical music. The Veena is named after Bobbili, a place where it was invented. In 2011 the musical instrument got a Geographical Indication tag from the Government of India.

title: Bones
blurb: The bones, also known as rhythm bones, are a folk instrument that, in their original form, consists of a pair of animal bones, but may also be played on pieces of wood or similar material.

title: Bulbul tarang
blurb: The Bulbul Tarang literally "waves of nightingales", alternately Indian Banjo) is a string instrument from India, that evolved from the Japanese taishōgoto, which likely arrived in South Asia in the 1930s. The Bulbul Tarang has evolved through the time.

title: Bullroarer
blurb: The bullroarer, rhombus, or turndun is an ancient ritual musical instrument and a device historically used for communicating over great distances. It consists of a piece of wood attached to a string, which when swung in a large circle produces a roaring vibration sound.

title: Cajón
blurb: A wooden box drum from Peru that the player sits on and slaps with the hands.

title: Calliope
blurb: 'Margie' Performed on the steam calliope of the Str. Julia Belle Swain Problems playing this file? See media help.

title: Chenda
blurb: The chenda is a cylindrical percussion instrument originating in the state of Kerala and widely used in Tulu Nadu of Karnataka in India. In Tulu Nadu, it is known as chende. The instrument is strongly associated with the cultural identity of both Kerala and Tulu Nadu.

title: Chimta
blurb: Chimta literally means tongs. Over time it has evolved into a traditional musical instrument of South Asia by the permanent addition of small brass jingles. This instrument is often used in popular Punjabi folk songs, Bhangra music and the Sikh religious music known as Gurbani Kirtan.

title: Collings Guitars
about: Handmade guitars and mandolins from Austin, Texas
blurb: A team of luthiers building custom handmade acoustic, electric and archtop guitars and mandolins in Austin, Texas.

title: Daf
about: Frame drum originating in Central Asia and the Middle East
blurb: The daf, also known as dap, dâyere or riq, is an Iranian frame drum musical instrument, also used in popular and classical music in Persian-influenced South Asia and Central Asia, such as in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Uzbekistan, Turkey many regions of Georgia, Armenia, Pakistan as…

title: Damaru
blurb: A damaru is a small two-headed drum used in Hinduism and Tibetan Buddhism. In Hinduism, the damaru is known as the instrument of the Hindu deity Shiva, associated with Tantric traditions.

title: Deering Banjo Company
about: Banjos made in the USA since 1975
blurb: The makers of Deering, Vega, Goodtime and Tenbrooks banjos, building 4-, 5- and 6-string banjos in the USA since 1975.

title: Dhak
about: Musical instrument from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: Durga Puja Dhak Sample Sound A 1:38 minute sample of Dhak playing during Durga Puja. Problems playing this file? See media help. The dhak is a huge membranophone instrument from Bengal and Assam. The shapes differ from the almost cylindrical to the barrel.

title: Dhol
blurb: A dhol Problems playing this file? See media help. Dhol can refer to any one of a number of similar types of double-headed drum widely used, with regional variations, throughout the Indian subcontinent.

title: Dholak
blurb: The dholak is a two-headed hand drum and folk percussion instrument of South Asian origin. The dholak can be anywhere about 16" to 24" in length.

title: Diddley bow
blurb: The diddley bow is a single-stringed American instrument that influenced the development of the blues sound. It consists of a single string of baling wire tensioned between two nails on a board over a glass bottle, which is used both as a bridge and as a means to amplify the instrument's sound.

title: Dotara
blurb: The dotara or dotar, is a two-stringed, plucked musical instrument from South Asia, with most contemporary models having four playing strings. Comparatively, the sarod is a slightly larger and more elaborate instrument, being built with an additional set of resonant sympathetic strings.

title: Dramyin
about: Himalayan folk music lute with six strings
blurb: The dramyin or dranyen is a traditional Himalayan folk music lute with six strings, used primarily as an accompaniment to singing in the Drukpa Buddhist culture and society in Bhutan, as well as in Tibet, Ladakh, Sikkim and Himalayan West Bengal.

title: Drum machine
about: Electronic musical instrument that creates percussion sounds
blurb: A drum machine is an electronic musical instrument that creates percussion sounds, drum beats, and patterns. Drum machines may imitate drum kits or other percussion instruments, or produce unique sounds, such as synthesized electronic tones.

title: Eight-string guitar
blurb: An eight-string guitar is a guitar with eight strings, or one more than the Russian guitar's seven. Eight-string guitars are less common than six- and seven-string guitars, but they are used by a few classical, jazz, and metal guitarists.

title: Ektara
blurb: The ektara is a one-stringed musical instrument used in the traditional music of Bengal, and used in modern-day music of Bangladesh, and eastern India. Two-stringed versions are called dotara, a name which also applies to another instrument of the same name.

title: Electric piano
blurb: An electric piano is a musical instrument that has a piano-style musical keyboard, where sound is produced by means of mechanical hammers striking metal strings or reeds or wire tines, which leads to vibrations which are then converted into electrical signals by pickups.

title: Electric sitar
blurb: An electric sitar is a type of electric string instrument designed to mimic the sound of the sitar, a traditional musical instrument of India. Depending on the manufacturer and model, these instruments bear varying degrees of resemblance to the traditional sitar.

title: Electronic drum
blurb: Electronic drums are an electronic musical instrument that replicates the sound and appearance of a drum kit or other percussion instruments.

title: Epiphone Casino
blurb: The Epiphone Casino is a thinline hollow body electric guitar manufactured by Epiphone, a branch of Gibson.

title: Esraj
about: String instrument from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The esraj or esraaj is a stringed instrument found in two forms throughout South Asia. It is a relatively recent instrument, being only about 300 years old.

title: Extended-range bass
about: Electric bass guitar with more than four strings
blurb: An extended-range bass is an electric bass guitar with a wider frequency range than a standard-tuned four-string bass guitar.

title: Fairlight CMI
blurb: The Fairlight CMI is a digital synthesizer, music sampler, and digital audio workstation introduced in 1979 by Fairlight. It was based on a commercial licence of the Qasar M8 developed by Tony Furse of Creative Strategies in Sydney, Australia.

title: Fender Esquire
about: Solid-body electric guitar manufactured by Fender
blurb: The Fender Esquire is a solid-body electric guitar manufactured by the Fender Musical Instruments Corporation of Los Angeles. It was the first solid-bodied guitar marketed by the company, and made its debut in 1950.

title: Fender Jaguar
blurb: The Fender Jaguar is an electric guitar by Fender Musical Instruments characterized by an offset-waist body, a relatively unusual switching system with two separate circuits for lead and rhythm, and a short-scale 24" neck.

title: Fender Jazz Bass
blurb: The Fender Jazz Bass is the second model of electric bass guitar created by Leo Fender. It is distinct from the Precision Bass in that its tone is brighter and richer in the midrange and treble with less emphasis on the fundamental frequency.

title: Fender Jazzmaster
blurb: The Fender Jazzmaster is an electric guitar designed as a more expensive sibling of the Fender Stratocaster. First introduced at the 1958 NAMM Convention, it was initially marketed to jazz guitarists, but found favor among surf rock guitarists in the early 1960s.

title: Fender Precision Bass
blurb: The Fender Precision Bass is an electric bass guitar model manufactured by Fender since 1951. The Precision Bass is a solid body, four-stringed, full scale bass guitar equipped with a single pickup and a 20-fret maple neck.

title: Fender Stratocaster
blurb: The contoured, three-pickup electric guitar of 1954, played by Hendrix, Clapton and millions since.

title: Flapamba
blurb: The flapamba is a musical instrument in the percussion family. It consists of tuned wooden bars pinched on one side over the node and mounted over resonator boxes. Sliding the bars slightly forward or backward affects their tuning.

title: Foot drum
blurb: A foot drum is any type of drum that is typically played by striking it with the bare foot or pedal and beater combination. The most common type of foot drum is the kick drum or bass drum of a drum set or trap kit, which consists of a deep cylindrical shell with drumheads attached to both ends.

title: Frankenstein
about: Electric guitar created by Eddie Van Halen
blurb: Frankenstein, also known as "Frankie", is a guitar created by Eddie Van Halen. Frankenstein was Van Halen's attempt to combine the sound of a classic Gibson guitar with the physical attributes and tremolo bar functionality of a Fender Stratocaster.

title: Frying Pan
blurb: The Rickenbacker Electro A-22, nicknamed the "Frying Pan", is the first electric lap steel guitar, also widely considered the first commercially successful electric guitar. Developed in 1931/1932, it received its patent in August 1937.

title: Ghatam
blurb: The ghaṭam is a percussion instrument used in various repertoires across the Indian subcontinent, especially in Southern India. Its variant is played in Punjab and known as gharha as it is a part of Punjabi folk traditions. Its analogue in Rajasthan is known as the madga and pani mataqa.

title: Ghungroo
about: Musical anklet tied to the feet of classical Indian dancers
blurb: A ghungroo, also known as gungjakal, ghunghru, ghungur or ghungura in Northern India, and chilanka, salangai, sadangai or gejje in the South, is one of many small metallic bells strung together to form ghungroos, a musical anklet tied to the feet of classical Indian dancers.

title: Gibson EDS-1275
blurb: The Gibson EDS-1275 is a double neck Gibson electric guitar introduced in 1958 and still in production. Popularized and raised to iconic status by musicians such as John McLaughlin, Don Felder, and Jimmy Page, it has been called "the coolest guitar in rock".

title: Gibson ES-335
blurb: The Gibson ES-335 is a semi-hollow body semi-acoustic guitar introduced by the Gibson Guitar Corporation as part of its ES series in 1958.

title: Gibson Explorer
blurb: The Gibson Explorer is a type of electric guitar model by Gibson guitars, released in 1958. The Explorer offered a radical, "futuristic" body design, much like its siblings the Flying V, which was released the same year, and the Moderne, which was designed in 1957 but not released until 1982.

title: Gibson Flying V
blurb: The Gibson Flying V is an electric guitar model introduced by Gibson in 1958. The Flying V offered a radical, "futuristic" body design, much like its siblings: the Explorer, which was released the same year, and the Moderne, which was designed in 1957 but not released until 1982.

title: Gibson Les Paul
blurb: A heavy, solid-bodied electric guitar with a thick, sustaining tone and a carved maple top.

title: Gibson SG
blurb: The Gibson SG, also known as Gibson Solid Guitar, is a solid-body electric guitar model introduced by Gibson in 1961, following on from the 1952 Gibson Les Paul. It remains in production in multiple variations of the initial design. SG stands for "solid guitar".

title: Glass harmonica
blurb: The glass harmonica, also known as the glass armonica, glass harmonium, bowl organ, hydrocrystalophone, or simply the armonica or harmonica is a type of musical instrument that uses a series of glass bowls or goblets graduated in size to produce musical tones by means of friction.

title: Greeny
blurb: Greeny is a 1959 Gibson Les Paul Standard, named after its first famous owner, Peter Green in 1964/5. He used it during his time in John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers and Fleetwood Mac, before selling it to Gary Moore in the early 1970s.

title: Gretsch 6120
about: Electric guitar made by Gretsch Guitars
blurb: The Gretsch 6120 is a hollow body electric guitar with f-holes, manufactured by Gretsch and first appearing in the mid-1950s with the endorsement of Chet Atkins.

title: Gretsch White Falcon
blurb: The Gretsch White Falcon is an electric hollow-body guitar introduced in 1954 by Gretsch. This guitar was created as a "showpiece" to exhibit the craft of Gretsch's luthiers, sales, and demonstration representative, Jimmie Webster, who created it for the 1954 NAMM Convention.

title: Groan tube
about: Toy that produces a sound when turned on one end
blurb: A groan tube is a toy that, when turned on one end, makes a distinct "groan" sound. This is due to a noise maker in the tube that vibrates in the air as it falls, making the noise.

title: Guitar synthesizer
about: Electronic system to modify guitar sound
blurb: A guitar synthesizer is any one of a number of musical systems that allow a guitarist to access synthesizer capabilities.

title: Hammered dulcimer
blurb: Hammered dulcimers are percussion-string instruments that share a common build of string-stretched trapezoidal resonant sound boards struck with small spoon-like mallets or hammers in each hand to produce sound.

title: Hammond organ
blurb: The Hammond organ is an electric organ invented by Laurens Hammond and John M. Hanert, first manufactured in 1935. Multiple models have been produced, most of which use sliding drawbars to vary sounds.

title: Ibanez RG
about: Series of electric guitars produced by Hoshino Gakki
blurb: The Ibanez RG is a series of electric guitars produced by Hoshino Gakki. The first model in the series, the RG550, was originally released in 1987 and advertised as part of the Roadstar series. That series was renamed "RG" in 1992 and all models since are simply known as RGs.

title: Idakka
blurb: The idakka, also spelt idaykka/edaykka/edakka, is an hourglass-shaped drum from Kerala in south India, very similar to the pan-Indian damaru. While the damaru is played by rattling knotted cords against the resonators, the idakka is played with a stick.

title: Instrument 1
about: Multi-instrument MIDI controller designed by Artiphon
blurb: The Instrument 1 is a MIDI controller designed by Artiphon, a Nashville-based music technology startup. The device was conceptualised in 2011 by Mike Butera, a fiddle player with a PhD in sound studies from Virginia Tech.

title: Jal tarang
blurb: The jal tarang is a melodic percussion instrument that originates from the Indian subcontinent. It consists of a set of ceramic or metal bowls filled with water. The bowls are played by striking the edge with beaters, one in each hand.

title: Jug
about: Musical instrument, based on an empty jug
blurb: The jug used as a musical instrument is an empty jug played with buzzed lips to produce a trombone-like tone. The characteristic sound of the jug is low and hoarse, below the higher pitch of the fiddle, harmonica, and the other instruments in the band.

title: Kalimba
blurb: A thumb piano: metal tines on a wooden board, plucked to make a soft, bell-like sound.

title: Kanileʻa ʻUkulele
blurb: Kanileʻa makes ʻukulele and guitars in Hawaiʻi, and works to restore native habitats on Hawaiʻi Island.

title: Kanjira
blurb: The kanjira, khanjira, khanjiri or ganjira, a South Indian frame drum, is an instrument of the tambourine family. As a folk and bhajan instrument, it has been used in the Indian subcontinent for many centuries.

title: Kazoo
blurb: The kazoo is a musical instrument that adds a buzzing timbral quality to a player's voice when the player vocalizes into it.

title: Khol
blurb: The khol is a terracotta two-sided drum used in northern and eastern India for accompaniment with devotional music. It is also known as a mridanga, not to be confused with mridangam. It originates from the Indian states of Odisha, West Bengal, Assam and Manipur.

title: Kinnari veena
blurb: The kinnari vina is a historical veena, a tube zither with gourds attached to act as resonators and frets. It was played in India into the late 19th century and was documented by two European artists. The instrument dates back into medieval times and possibly as far back as 500 C.E.

title: Korg MS-10
blurb: The Korg MS-10 is an analogue synthesizer created by Korg in 1978. Unlike its bigger brother, the Korg MS-20, the MS-10 only has one VCO, one VCF and one envelope generator. It is monophonic and has 32 keys. The MS-10 is well known for its huge sounding electro bass sounds.

title: Lujon
about: Musical instrument in the percussion family
blurb: The lujon is a bass metallophone consisting of individually-pitched metal plates that are attached to the resonance chambers of a partitioned wooden box.

title: Mellotron
blurb: The Mellotron is an electro-mechanical musical instrument developed in Birmingham, England, in 1963. It is played by pressing its keys, each of which causes a length of magnetic tape to contact a capstan, which pulls it across a playback head.

title: Minimoog
blurb: The Minimoog is an analog synthesizer introduced by Moog Music in 1970. Designed as a more affordable, portable version of the modular Moog synthesizer, it was the first synthesizer sold in retail stores.

title: Mohan veena
about: Plucked string instrument used in Indian classical music
blurb: Mohan veena refers to either of two distinct plucked string instruments used in Indian classical music, especially Hindustani classical music which is associated with the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent.

title: Moog synthesizer
blurb: The 1960s modular synthesizer, all patch cables and knobs, that brought electronic sound into pop music.

title: Morsing
about: Instrument played with the help of mouth and hand
blurb: The morsing is an instrument similar to the Jew's harp, mainly used in Rajasthan of North India, in the Carnatic music of South India, in Nepal, and in Sindh, Pakistan. It can be categorized under lamellophones, which is a sub-category of plucked idiophones.

title: Mridangam
blurb: The mridangam is an ancient percussion instrument originating from the Indian subcontinent. It is a traditional royal instrument originating in the south Indian state of Tamil Nadu and is widely used in south Indian classical music, called Carnatic music.

title: Nadaswaram
blurb: The nadaswaram is a double reed wind instrument from Tamil Nadu. It is used as a traditional classical instrument in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala and in the northern and eastern parts of Sri Lanka.

title: Nafir
about: Natural trumpet, dates to ancient/medieval periods, straight tube with a bell
blurb: The nafir is a slender, shrill-sounding straight natural trumpet with a cylindrical tube and a conical metal bell, producing one or two notes.

title: Naqareh
about: Middle Eastern drum with a rounded back and a hide head
blurb: The naqareh, naqqāra, nagara or nagada is a Middle Eastern drum with a rounded back and a hide head, usually played in pairs. It is thus a membranophone of the kettle drum variety.

title: Oberheim DMX
blurb: The DMX is a programmable digital drum machine manufactured by Oberheim. It was introduced in 1980 at a list price of US$2,895 and remained in the company's product line until the mid-1980s.

title: Ocarina
blurb: A rounded clay vessel flute with finger holes, thousands of years old and famous again thanks to a video game.

title: Omnichord
blurb: The Omnichord is an electronic musical instrument introduced in 1981 by the Suzuki Musical Instrument Corporation. Conceived as an electronic autoharp, it allows users to play harp-like arpeggios produced through an electronic strum plate, simulating the experience of playing a stringed instrument.

title: Ondes Martenot
blurb: The ondes Martenot or ondes musicales is an early electronic musical instrument. Early models were played only by moving a ring tied to a wire, creating "wavering" sounds similar to a theremin, but a lateral-vibrato keyboard was soon added.

title: Otamatone
blurb: The Otamatone is an electronic musical synthesizer. Shaped like an eighth note, the ribbon controller on its stem is used to control pitch, while the notes produced by the synthesizer are played from the Otamatone's "head".

title: Pakhavaj
blurb: The pakhavaj or pakhawaj is a barrel-shaped, two-headed drum, originating from the Indian subcontinent, kendang of Maritime Southeast Asia and other Indian double-headed drums. Its older forms were made with clay.

title: Parai
blurb: Parai also known as Thappattai or Thappu is a traditional percussion instrument from South India, used to make announcements and played during festivals, folk dances, weddings and functions.

title: Pedal steel guitar
blurb: The pedal steel guitar is a string instrument mounted horizontally on a frame and played while seated. The player typically plucks the strings with the right hand while moving a steel bar along the strings with the left.

title: Puerto Rican cuatro
blurb: The Puerto Rican cuatro is the national instrument of Puerto Rico. It belongs to the lute family of string instruments, and is guitar-like in function, but with a shape closer to that of the violin.

title: Pungi
about: Wind instrument originating from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The pungi, also known as bīn or Murli, is a musical instrument that originates from the Indian subcontinent. The instrument consists of a reservoir into which air is blown and then channelled into two reed pipes. It is played with no pauses, as the player employs circular breathing.

title: Rainstick
blurb: A rainstick is a long, hollow tube of bamboo or dried cactus that is partially flooded with small pebbles, rice, dried beans, or other hard granular matter. The inside surface of the tube has small pins or thorns arranged helically.

title: Ransingha
blurb: The ransingha or ransinga is a type of primitive trumpet made of copper or copper alloys, used in both India and Nepal. The instrument is made of two metal curves, joined to form an "S" shape. It may also be reassembled to form a crescent.

title: Ravanahatha
blurb: A ravanahatha is an ancient bowed, stringed instrument, used in India, Sri Lanka, and surrounding areas. It has been suggested as an ancestor of the violin.

title: Red Special
about: Electric guitar played by Brian May
blurb: The Red Special is the electric guitar designed and built by Queen's guitarist Brian May and his father, Harold, when Brian was a teenager in the early 1960s. The Red Special is sometimes referred to as the Fireplace or the Old Lady by May and by others.

title: Rhodes piano
blurb: The Rhodes piano is an electric piano invented by Harold Rhodes, which became popular in the 1970s. Like a conventional piano, the Rhodes generates sound with keys and hammers, but instead of strings, the hammers strike thin metal tines, which vibrate next to an electromagnetic pickup.

title: Rickenbacker 325
blurb: The Rickenbacker 325 is the first of the Capri series of hollow body guitars released in 1958 by Rickenbacker.

title: Rickenbacker 360/12
blurb: The Rickenbacker 360/12 is the Rickenbacker company's 12-string variant of its 360 electric guitar model. Mainly known for producing "jangly" sounds, it was among the first electric 12-string guitars.

title: Rikhi Ram
about: Indian instruments from Connaught Place, New Delhi
blurb: The Rikhi Ram Musical Instrument Manufacturing Co. makes and sells Indian musical instruments from its store in Connaught Circus, New Delhi.

title: Roland TB-303
blurb: The Roland TB-303 Bass Line is a bass synthesizer released by Roland Corporation in 1981. Designed to simulate bass guitars, it was a commercial failure and was discontinued in 1984.

title: Roland TR-808
blurb: The Roland TR-808 Rhythm Composer, commonly known as the 808, is a drum machine manufactured by Roland Corporation between 1980 and 1983. It was one of the first drum machines to allow users to program rhythms instead of using preset patterns.

title: Rubab
blurb: The rubab or robab is a lute-like musical instrument of Central Asian origin. It is the national musical instrument of Afghanistan and is also commonly played in India and Pakistan, mostly by Balochis and Kashmiris, and Punjabis.

title: Rudra veena
blurb: The rudra veena, also called the bīn in North India, is a large plucked string instrument used in Hindustani music, especially dhrupad. It is one of the major types of veena played in Indian classical music, notable for its deep bass resonance.

title: Santa Cruz Guitar Company
blurb: Acoustic guitars handcrafted in California since 1976.

title: Saraswati veena
blurb: The Sarasvatī vīṇa is an ancient Indian plucked veena. It is named after the Hindu goddess Saraswati, who is usually depicted holding or playing the instrument. Also known as raghunatha veena, it is used mostly in Carnatic Indian classical music.

title: Seven-string guitar
blurb: The seven-string guitar adds one string to the more common six-string guitar, commonly used to extend the bass range or also to extend the treble range.

title: Shankha
about: End-blown conch trumpet of Indian origin
blurb: A Shankha has religious ritual importance in Hinduism. In Hinduism, the shankha called panchajanya is a sacred emblem of the Hindu preserver deity Vishnu. It is still used as a trumpet in Hindu ritual, and in the past was used as a war trumpet.

title: Shruti box
blurb: A shruti box is a musical instrument, originating from the Indian subcontinent, that traditionally works on a system of bellows. It is similar to a harmonium and is used to provide a drone in a practice session or concert of Indian classical music.

title: Sitar
blurb: A long-necked Indian lute with sympathetic strings that shimmer under the melody.

title: Song bells
blurb: Song bells are a musical instrument in the keyboard percussion family. They are a mallet percussion instrument in the metallophone family that is essentially a cross between the vibraphone, glockenspiel, and celesta. They have bars made of aluminum.

title: Sousaphone
blurb: The sousaphone is a brass musical instrument in the tuba family. It was first created around 1893 by J. W. Pepper as a modification of the helicon, at the direction of American bandleader John Philip Sousa, after whom the instrument was named.

title: Steel guitar
about: Type of guitar or the method of playing the instrument
blurb: A steel guitar is a guitar played while moving a steel bar or similar hard object against plucked strings. The bar itself is called a "steel" and is the source of the name "steel guitar". The instrument differs from a conventional guitar in that it has no frets—but markers that look like frets.

title: Steelpan
blurb: A tuned drum hammered out of an oil barrel in Trinidad, sounding like sunshine.

title: Stradivarius
about: String instruments built by the Stradivari family, particularly Antonio
blurb: A Stradivarius is a string instrument, such as a violin, viola, cello, or guitar, crafted during the late 17th and early 18th centuries by Antonio Stradivari and other members of the Stradivari family in Cremona, Italy.

title: Stylophone
blurb: The Stylophone is a miniature analog synthesizer played with a stylus. Invented in 1967 by Brian Jarvis, it entered production in 1968 and was manufactured by Dubreq in London. Around three million units were sold during its original production run.

title: Superstrat
blurb: Superstrat is a name for an electric guitar design that resembles a Fender Stratocaster but with differences that clearly distinguish it from a standard Stratocaster, usually to cater to a different playing style.

title: Taal
about: Cymbal originated from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The taal or manjira, jalra, karatala, kartal or gini is a pair of clash cymbals, originating in the Indian subcontinent, which make high-pitched percussion sounds. In its simplest form, it consists of a pair of small hand cymbals.

title: Tabla
about: Pair of hand drums from South Asia
blurb: The tabla is a pair of hand drums from South Asia, particularly the Indian subcontinent. Since the 18th century, it has been the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music, where it may be played solo, as an accompaniment with other instruments and vocals, or as a part of larger…

title: Tanpura
blurb: The tanpura; also referred to as tambura, tanpuri, tamboura, or tanpoura) is a long-necked, plucked, four-stringed instrument originating in the Indian subcontinent, found in various forms in Indian music.

title: Taus
blurb: The taus, also known as the mayuri veena, is a bowed string instrument from North India. It is a form of veena used in North India with a peacock-shaped resonator called a mayuri, and is played with the neck of the instrument on bow.

title: The Black Strat
blurb: The Black Strat is a black 1969 Fender Stratocaster guitar played by the English guitarist David Gilmour of the progressive rock band Pink Floyd. It appeared for the first time with Gilmour at the 1970 Bath Festival.

title: Theatre organ
about: Style of pipe organ used for entertainment
blurb: A theatre organ, also known as a theater organ or cinema organ in the United Kingdom, is a type of pipe organ developed to accompany silent films from the 1900s to the 1920s.

title: Theremin
blurb: An electronic instrument played without touching it, by moving your hands near two antennas.

title: Trigger
blurb: Trigger is a modified Martin N-20 nylon-string classical acoustic guitar used by country music singer-songwriter Willie Nelson. Early in his career, Nelson tested several guitars by different companies.

title: Tumbi
blurb: The tumbi or toombi, also called a tumba or toomba, is a traditional musical instrument from the Punjab region of the northern Indian subcontinent. The high-pitched, single-string plucking instrument is associated with folk music of Punjab and presently very popular in Western Bhangra music.

title: Twelve-string guitar
about: Fretted string instrument optimized for richer sounds
blurb: A twelve-string guitar is a steel-string guitar with 12 strings in six courses, which produces a thicker, more ringing tone than a standard six-string guitar. Typically, the strings of the lower four courses are tuned in octaves, with those of the upper two courses tuned in unison.

title: Veena
about: Various chordophone instruments from the Indian subcontinent
blurb: The veena, also spelled vina, is any of various chordophone instruments from the Indian subcontinent. Ancient musical instruments evolved into many variations, such as lutes, zithers and arched harps.

title: Vest frottoir
about: Percussion instrument used in zydeco music
blurb: A vest frottoir or vest rubboard is a percussion instrument used in zydeco music similar to a washboard. It is usually made from pressed, corrugated stainless steel and is worn over the shoulders. It is played as a rhythm instrument by being stroked downward with either bottle openers or spoons.

title: Vibraphone
blurb: Vibraphone sound sample An F major scale played on a vibraphone with the motors on Problems playing this file? See media help. The vibraphone is a percussion instrument in the metallophone family. It consists of tuned metal bars and is typically played by using mallets to strike the bars.

title: Vibraslap
blurb: The vibraslap is a percussion instrument consisting of a piece of stiff wire connecting a wooden ball to a hollow box of wood with metal “teeth” inside. The percussionist holds the metal wire in one hand and strikes the ball.

title: Washboard
blurb: The washboard and frottoir are used as a percussion instrument, employing the ribbed metal surface of the cleaning device as a rhythm instrument.

title: Yamaha DX7
blurb: The Yamaha DX7 is a synthesizer introduced by Yamaha Corporation in 1983. It was the first successful digital synthesizer and is one of the best-selling synthesizers in history, selling more than 200,000 units. In the early 1980s, the synthesizer market was dominated by analog synthesizers.

title: Yazh
blurb: The yazh is a harp used in ancient Tamil music. It was strung with gut strings that ran from a curved ebony neck to a boat or trough-shaped resonator, the opening of which was covered with skin for a soundboard.
